Baseline Topology

1. What is Baseline Topology?
  • The Baseline Topology (BLT) is the set of server nodes that are expected to store persistent data;
  • It only matters when Native Persistence is enabled;
  • Ignite will not activate the cluster until all nodes in the baseline topology are present;
  • This prevents the cluster from starting with partial data after a restart;
2. Why is it needed?
  • Without BLT, if only 2 of 5 nodes restart, the cluster would activate and serve incomplete data;
  • BLT ensures the cluster waits until all expected nodes are online before becoming active;
  • It also controls data rebalancing — data is only rebalanced when the BLT changes, not on every transient topology event;
3. Managing the Baseline Topology
  • Set via the control script: 
    # View current baseline
$IGNITE_HOME/bin/control.sh --baseline

# Add a node to the baseline
$IGNITE_HOME/bin/control.sh --baseline add consistentId1,consistentId2

# Remove a node from the baseline
$IGNITE_HOME/bin/control.sh --baseline remove consistentId1

# Set a specific baseline topology
$IGNITE_HOME/bin/control.sh --baseline set consistentId1,consistentId2,consistentId3
  • Set programmatically: 
    ignite.cluster().setBaselineTopology(ignite.cluster().forServers().nodes());
4. Auto-Adjust Baseline
  • Ignite can automatically adjust the baseline after a timeout when nodes join or leave: 
    ignite.cluster().baselineAutoAdjustEnabled(true);
ignite.cluster().baselineAutoAdjustTimeout(30_000); // 30 seconds
  • This avoids manual baseline management at the cost of potential rebalancing on transient node departures;
  • Enabled by default since Ignite 2.8;
5. Consistent ID
  • Each server node has a consistent ID — a unique identifier that persists across restarts;
  • By default, it is derived from the node's IP address and discovery port;
  • You can set it explicitly: 
    IgniteConfiguration cfg = new IgniteConfiguration();
cfg.setConsistentId("node-1");
  • The consistent ID is used to identify nodes in the baseline topology and to map partitions to nodes;
